selected_passages.text: Google CEO Sundar Pichai testified in a U.S. antitrust trial defending the company's $26.3 billion spending to secure default search engine status across platforms, including a major deal with Apple. selected_passages.title: sources/Apple_defends_Google_Search_deal_in_court_There_wasn_t_a_valid_alternative
selected_passages.text:
- Eddy Cue testified that there was no valid alternative to Google Search for Apple devices at the time of the deal.
- The Information Services Agreement (ISA) makes Google the default search engine on Apple products in exchange for billions in payments.
- Apple believes in protecting user privacy but also maintains a strong partnership with Google, creating a central tension in the trial.
- Cue argued that showing users alternative search engines during setup would degrade the user experience and slow down device onboarding.
- The Justice Department questions whether Apple's choice of Google is based on product quality or financial incentives.

selected_passages.title: sources/News_publisher_files_class_action_antitrust_suit_against_Google_citing_AI_s_harms_to_their_bottom_line
selected_passages.text:
- The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court in D.C.
- Helena World Chronicle owns two weekly newspapers in Arkansas.
- Google's Search Generative Experience (SGE) is cited as worsening the problem.
- Google's Bard AI chatbot is cited as worsening the problem.
- The Knowledge Graph was launched in May 2012.
- By 2020, the Knowledge Graph contained 500 billion facts about 5 billion entities.
- Google drives nearly 40% of The Atlantic's traffic.
- The Atlantic modeled that AI would answer 75% of queries without a click-through.
- Publishers believe they will lose 20-40% of website traffic from Google's AI rollout.
- Axel Springer licensed news to OpenAI for AI model training.
- GoogleBot is the crawler used for both general search and SGE.
- Google paid $73.5 million (100 million Canadian dollars) to Canadian news organizations.
- Meta began blocking news in Canada in August.
- The U.S. Justice Department filed a separate antitrust suit against Google.
- The 2020 Justice Department suit was over search and search advertising.
- Epic Games won a recent lawsuit against Google over app store antitrust issues.
- Google links people to publisher websites more than 24 billion times monthly.
- News and Media sites were the third largest category of AI training data.
- The law firm handling the case is Hausfeld.
